Yiran Zhang
Research Robotics Publications

Yiran Zhang

AI agent evaluation · Singapore

I work on AI agent evaluation. My research background spans adversarial testing, uncertainty monitoring, and human–machine collaboration, alongside hands-on work with robotic systems.

My research at Nanyang Technological University has explored how to expose failures, assess reliability, and support decisions under uncertainty in autonomous systems.

I am also interested in opportunities in robotics and embodied intelligence.

Selected research

Prior work in stress testing, reliability monitoring, and human–machine interaction.

Prediction & planning

OOD-Aware Joint Prediction and Planning for Autonomous Driving with Contrastive Learning and Reconstruction-Based Filtering

Yiran Zhang, Hui Shi, Shanhe Lou, Chen Lv

Under review

Filtering unreliable plans. Counterfactual training, contrastive similarity, and reconstruction errors help identify unreliable prediction-and-planning candidates. The best variant achieved 85.3% successful accomplishment in the aggregated evaluation; conservative fallback can still cause unnecessary stops.

Enlarge ↗

Runtime monitoring

A Robust Guardian for Autonomous Driving with Game-Theoretic and Diffusion Counterfactuals

Yiran Zhang, Shanhe Lou, Hui Shi, Chen Lv

Transportation Research Part C · 2026

A monitor that knows its own uncertainty. Game-theoretic and diffusion counterfactuals train a guardian to detect unfamiliar situations and support contingency re-planning. Evaluation covers multiple datasets, traffic environments, and three planner types.

Paper ↗

Adversarial testing

Adversarial Traffic Scene Generation Considering Harm, Rarity, and Ambiguity for Autonomous Driving Testing

Yiran Zhang, Shanhe Lou, Baichuan Lou, Haitao Zhang, Chen Lv

Transportation Research Part C · 2025

Stress tests beyond average-case performance. Adversarial scenes target harm, rarity, and ambiguity, combining game-theoretic interactions with uncertainty-based objectives. Evaluations test how effectively these scenes expose vulnerabilities in both optimization-based and learning-based planners.

Paper ↗

Runtime monitoring

A Planner-agnostic Monitor for Behaviour Feasibility of Autonomous Vehicles Using a Bayesian Discriminator

Yiran Zhang, Zhongxu Hu, Haohan Yang, Shanhe Lou, Chen Lv

IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems · 2025

Reliability checks across different planners. MonitorGAN uses a Bayesian discriminator to assess plan feasibility and estimate its own uncertainty, without real outlier exposure during training. Cross-dataset experiments cover learning-based, polynomial-based, and optimization-based planners.

Paper ↗

Adaptation & interaction

Interactive Prediction and Decision-Making for Autonomous Vehicles: Online Active Learning with Traffic Entropy Minimization

Yiran Zhang, Shanhe Lou, Peng Hang, Wenhui Huang, Lie Yang, Chen Lv

IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems · 2024

Adapting predictions from partial feedback. Online learning updates a fixed predictor as new interactions unfold, while traffic-entropy minimization encourages more predictable decisions. Human-in-the-loop and cross-dataset experiments evaluate reliability under uncertain road-user behaviour.

Paper ↗

Human–machine collaboration

Socially-Compliant Hierarchical Human-Vehicle Collaboration with Multimodal Haptic Steering

Yiran Zhang, Shanhe Lou, Zhongxu Hu, Jieyu Zhu, Chen Lv

IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems · 2025

Connecting human decisions with control feedback. A shared-driving framework combines interaction-aware prediction, human guidance, and haptic steering. Human-in-the-loop experiments assess human–machine conflict and safety under dynamically allocated control authority.

Human–machine collaboration

Human-Machine Cooperative Decision-making and Planning for Automated Vehicles Using Spatial Projection of Hand Gestures

Yiran Zhang, Zhongxu Hu, Peng Hang, Shanhe Lou, Chen Lv

Advanced Engineering Informatics · 2024

High-level guidance through a visual interface. Hand gestures are projected onto the road to guide cooperative decision-making and planning. Experiments compare driving performance and physical and mental workload with conventional manual guidance.

Human–machine interaction

Shutoko Highway: Autonomous Driving & Human–Machine Interface

Systems demonstration

An integrated autonomous-driving and human–machine interface demonstration. The project investigates situations in which passengers do not trust the driving algorithm, with the aim of informing more personalized driving behaviour. The work includes the driving algorithm and the interaction interfaces.

Naturalistic testing

Human-like Interactive Behavior Generation for Autonomous Vehicles: A Bayesian Game-theoretic Approach with Turing Test

Yiran Zhang, Peng Hang, Chao Huang, Chen Lv

Advanced Intelligent Systems · 2022

Human-like behaviour for interactive testing. A Bayesian game model captures road-user interaction under uncertain intentions, including probing behaviour. Simulation experiments and Turing tests evaluate the human-likeness of the generated scenes.
